title: Stressed-host actor-mesh performance-signature calibration (design + ladder plan)
purpose: Re-verify the MAXIMUM ACHIEVABLE streaming-to-disk (the MPRR visual-ring frame->disk ceiling) under a STRESSED host while a MESH of actors each runs at a DIFFERENT stress level, with the full 42-counter performance schema instrumented PER ACTOR, to gather the initial metadata needed to design + calibrate a PERFORMANCE SIGNATURE calibrator for later LADDER testing.
buildsOn: MPRR visual ring (ADR-0005 image-storage ring buffer, ADR-0007 image-derived timing, ADR-0009 absorb-MPRR)
existing mesh infra: experiments/ephemeral-mesh, experiments/multi-vm-topology, experiments/mesh-runs, experiments/mprr-ring

placement.where: ALL actors on THIS host (VMs) -- no separate WIN plane for this program
placement.planes: both a Windows actor mesh and a Linux actor mesh run here (Windows guests + Linux guests)
placement.hostBudget: recorded per run (this host ~ 60 GB RAM / 24 CPUs; ~24 GB free with 2 VMs up). Mesh size N is chosen so N actor VMs + the host stressor fit without host thrash; recorded in the receipt.
placement.counterMappingNote: the 42-counter catalog is Windows PDH. Linux actors sample the EQUIVALENT counters from /proc + /sys (cpu, mem, disk via /proc/diskstats, net via /proc/net/dev, per-process via /proc/<pid>/stat|io) mapped onto the same catalog keys; counters with no Linux analogue sample null and are skipped.

maxDiskStreaming.target: MPRR visual-ring buffer sustained frame->disk write throughput -- the MAX ACHIEVABLE before the ring back-pressures or drops frames.

metric.dropFreeCeilingFps: highest sustained frames/sec the ring writes to disk with ZERO dropped frames
metric.backpressureOnsetEpochMs: first epoch where ring occupancy hits the high-water mark

maxDiskStreaming.reverify: Re-run the streaming benchmark while sampling ALL 42 counters per actor and correlating each sample to the 12 FPS frame timeline (performance-counter-correlation@v2). REFRESH the committed receipt as the posted evidence.
maxDiskStreaming.note: the ceiling is expected to MOVE as host + per-actor stress rises -- that movement vs stress is exactly the calibration signal.

hostLoad.role: background HOST pressure applied while the mesh acquires, so the actors measure themselves on a loaded host (not an idle one)

mechanisms: WORKLOAD: a stress-ng / synthetic workload INSIDE the actor VM sized to the level
THROTTLE: bound the level with a VirtualBox CPU execution cap (VBoxManage modifyvm --cpuexecutioncap) + an IO bandwidth limit (--bandwidthctl) / Linux cgroup io.max
perActorLevel.intent: in ONE acquisition each actor is pinned to a DIFFERENT level so a single mesh run spans the stress range (a horizontal slice across the ladder).
perActorLevel.invariant: the per-actor level is both COMMANDED (workload+throttle) and MEASURED (the 42-counter signature); calibration compares commanded vs measured.

signature.definition: A performance SIGNATURE fingerprints 'this actor at this stress level on this host' as the REPETITIVE (structural/periodic) and OUTLIER (anomalous) patterns extracted from the per-actor 42-counter series across MULTIPLE REPEATED benchmarks. Repeatable structure that survives repeats is the signature; what varies across repeats is the noise floor. Outliers carry post-processing information (visual root-cause).
crossCounterFeatures: counter pairs whose OUTLIERS co-occur within the +/-200 ms marker tolerance (a shared-cause signature)
signature.repetitionModel: run R repeats per (actor, level); a feature is SIGNATURE if its across-repeat coefficient-of-variation <= stabilityThreshold, else it is NOISE. The signature is the vector of stable features + the characteristic outlier profile.
signature.postProcessing: each outlier epoch becomes a frameMarker (frame-marker@v2, +/-200 ms image grab) so the captured frame at the anomaly can be pulled for visual root-cause -- ties this program back to the click-marker mechanism.

calibrator.input: signatures across the full LADDER of rungs (idle..saturate) x R repeats, per actor, per plane (Win/Linux).

output.calibrationCurve: per counter + per salient feature: stressRung -> expected value + tolerance band (from the across-repeat variance)
output.streamingCeilingCurve: the max drop-free streaming ceiling vs stress rung
output.inverseRead: map an OBSERVED signature back to an INFERRED stress level (the calibrated read) with a confidence from the band

calibrator.fit: monotone / piecewise-linear fit over the rungs; the across-repeat variance sets the band; NON-MONOTONE rungs are flagged as instrumentation artifacts (a counter that does not track stress is dropped from the signature).
designInvariants: monotone: salient signature features move monotonically with the stress rung (else flagged)
separable: adjacent rungs' bands do not fully overlap for at least K signature dimensions (the ladder is resolvable)
repeatable: across-repeat CoV <= stabilityThreshold for the signature dimensions

ladder.definition: LADDER testing = drive the mesh through INCREASING stress RUNGS to build a calibration curve, then later re-run the ladder and read each rung against the calibrated curve to detect drift/regression.
ladder.product: per-rung signatures = the calibration set -> the calibrator fits the curve. 'Later ladder testing' replays the ladder and scores each rung's signature vs the calibrated curve (pass = within band; fail = drift/regression).

evidence.receipt: will record: host budget, mesh size + per-actor commanded levels, the re-verified max drop-free streaming ceiling WITH all-42-counter correlation, the extracted per-(actor,level) signatures, the fitted calibration curve + ladder resolvability, and pass/fail vs the design invariants.
evidence.reverifyExisting: the existing max-streaming evidence (ADR-0005/0007, self-test-conformance receipts) is re-verified under the expanded schema and the refreshed numbers are posted here.

followUp: This schema is DESIGN-ONLY. The implementation follow-up (its own requirement + gate): the in-guest 42-counter samplers (Win PDH + Linux /proc), the stress orchestrator (host stress-ng + per-actor workload/throttle), the live Win & Linux mesh ladder runs, the signature extractor, and the calibration-curve fitter -- each a dependency-free engine + self-test + gate + a real receipt.
